standard_prerequisites.name: The preliminary preparation of the tame symbol in a finite extension
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, label lemma-prepare-tame-symbol, invoked at proof lines 913 and 933
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces, for the finitely many nonzerodivisors involved, a finite ring extension in which the elements become monomials in a single nonzerodivisor up to units, which reduces each verification to an identity among the units and the exponents.

core_obligations: Prove bilinearity: for nonzerodivisors a_1, a_2, a_3 choose the extension provided by the preparation lemma and verify the displayed identity of the local factors, namely that the signs and the unit contributions multiply correctly; the identities are immediate from the definition of the symbol in terms of exponents and units (proof lines 910-928).
Prove skew symmetry and the first normalization property in the same manner, since both are equally immediate after preparing the symbol (proof lines 927-928).

Prove the second normalization property: for nonzerodivisors a_1, a_2 and their difference, prepare the symbol again and reduce the required congruence modulo the maximal ideal to a case distinction on the exponents; if the three exponents agree the congruence is clear, and if one is larger the other two agree and the residue class of the corresponding unit is that of minus the other, so that the signs cancel; the remaining cases are the same, and this verification explains the choice of signs in the definition of the symbol (proof lines 930-948).
proof_roadmap: Prepare the symbol once for the three elements and verify bilinearity (proof lines 910-926).
Get skew symmetry and the first normalization property in the same way (proof lines 927-928).
Verify the second normalization property by a case distinction on exponents (proof lines 930-948).
difficulty_reason: The lemma verifies that the tame symbol defined earlier satisfies the five structural properties announced for it: bilinearity, skew symmetry, and three normalization statements, the last of which is the one that forces the particular sign in its definition (statement lines 901-908, tag 0EAS). The verifications are computations rather than citations: for each identity one first prepares the symbol in a finite extension where the elements are monomials up to units, and then checks an identity among exponents and unit contributions, with the final property needing a genuine case distinction on the exponents together with the observation that the residue class of one unit is minus that of another. The case distinction is the substance, so the claim is H2.
